description: The shared money/tolerance fixture referenced by docs/CONTRACT.md (Money section, PI reconciliation section). Source of truth lives here, in the backend repo; shvoy-frontend vendors an exact copy via scripts/sync-money-fixture.mjs. Both test suites (MoneyToleranceFixtureTest here; rounding.test.ts/percentage.test.ts there) assert every case against their own implementation — this is what makes cross-repo divergence fail in CI instead of surfacing during reconciliation with a live supplier. Every rounding case uses HALF_EVEN; every tolerance case uses the EXCLUSIVE boundary (`|variance| < tolerance`); variance is rounded HALF_EVEN to 2dp before it is stored, displayed, or compared — never against a raw value. See CONTRACT.md's Money and 'Tolerance evaluation & auto-confirm (Story 5.4)' sections for the prose.

orderTotals.description: three lines of 0.115 (3dp) — the classic sum-then-round-vs-round-then-sum divergence case
orderTotals.note: unrounded sum is 0.345, an exact tie at 2dp — HALF_EVEN picks 0.34 (even), widening the divergence from the HALF_UP fixture's 0.35

orderTotals.description: a typical PO with three distinct line items, two of which are themselves exact HALF_EVEN ties
orderTotals.note: 12.3450 is a tie resolved to 12.34 (even); 8.9950 is a tie resolved to 9.00 (even); 100.0025 isn't a tie and rounds down

depositBalanceSplit.description: classic 30/70 split of an odd amount — no tie, deposit rounds down normally
depositBalanceSplit.note: deposit = round(100.01 * 0.30, HALF_EVEN, 2dp) = 30.00 (30.003, not a tie); balance = total - deposit, never independently rounded

depositBalanceSplit.description: an exact tie in the deposit calculation itself — the tiebreak case
depositBalanceSplit.note: ideal deposit is 25.025, an exact tie between 25.02 and 25.03 — HALF_EVEN picks 25.02 (even). A naive 'round half up' or 'largest remainder, ties to first ratio' split would give 25.03/25.02 instead — this is the case that tells the two algorithms apart. There is no independent tiebreak rule for the balance: it always simply absorbs whatever the total minus the (already-decided) deposit leaves.

depositBalanceSplit.description: negative total, reachable via the credit ledger — same rule, sign carried through
depositBalanceSplit.note: mirrors the first case exactly with both parts negated; HALF_EVEN's tie-breaking is sign-symmetric so the same rounding decision applies to the magnitude regardless of sign

round-before-compare: the raw variance is genuinely below tolerance, but HALF_EVEN rounding of an exact tie pushes it to exactly the boundary, which then routes — deliberate, shipped behaviour, not a defect. A comparison against the raw 1.9950 would wrongly auto-confirm.
the same rounding-tie mechanism, resolving downward instead of upward — proves the mode is HALF_EVEN in both directions, not 'rounds up on ties'
